title: Metformin Use in PCOS Pregnancies Increases the Risk of Offspring Overweight at 4 Years of Age: Follow-Up of Two RCTs
authors: Hanem LGE, Stridsklev S, Juliusson PB, Salvesen O, Roelants M, Carlsen SM, et al.
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
followUp: anthropometry at birth, 6 months, 1, 1.5, 2 and 4 years of age
population: 182 children of 170 mothers with polycystic ovary syndrome who had taken part in two randomised trials of metformin in pregnancy at eleven public hospitals in Norway; 62% of the 292 invited children consented to participate
funder: This work was supported by the Research Council of Norway, which funded the follow-up study (registration number 239987), the NovoNordisk Foundation and Felles Forskningsutvalg.
authorConflicts: The authors have nothing to disclose.
result: Mothers had received metformin 1700 or 2000 mg daily or placebo from the first trimester to delivery in the original trials; there was no intervention in the follow-up. At 4 years of age the difference in height z score between groups was not significant (0.07, 95% CI -0.22 to 0.36, p = 0.651), while the metformin group had a higher weight z score (difference in means 0.38, 0.07 to 0.69, p = 0.017) and a higher body-mass index z score (0.45, 0.11 to 0.78, p = 0.010). More children were overweight or obese in the metformin group, 26 (32%) against 14 (18%) in the placebo group, odds ratio 2.17 (1.04 to 4.61, p = 0.038); the number needed to harm for an additional case of overweight or obesity at 4 years was 7. The difference in mean head circumference z score at 1 year was 0.27 (-0.04 to 0.58, p = 0.093). Data from all 182 children entered the mixed linear models, though the main outcomes at 4 years were missing for 21 children and head circumference at 1 year for 28. The authors note that participants were representative of women with a known diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome and that the results might not translate to mothers without the syndrome.
